seo.title: Join
seo.description: How to join IEEE EMBS at UCF, and what society membership adds — scholarships, member conference rates, journals, and speakers.

hero.headline: How to join
hero.lede: Come to a general body meeting and you're part of the chapter. Here's what people usually ask, and what IEEE EMBS membership adds on top.

faqs.question: What major do I need?
faqs.answer: Any engineering or science major. UCF doesn't offer an undergraduate biomedical engineering degree, so nobody here is one — our members come from electrical, mechanical, computer science, photonics, and elsewhere. The work is interdisciplinary because it has to be.

faqs.question: Do I need experience to be useful?
faqs.answer: No. Meetings and workshops are pitched at people seeing the material for the first time, and most of the learning happens next to someone a year or two ahead of you.

faqs.question: What does IEEE EMBS membership cost?
faqs.answer: IEEE student membership plus the EMBS society add-on, both set by IEEE and revised each year. It's the lowest rate you'll ever be offered, and it's what makes the scholarships, conference rates, and journals available to you.

faqs.question: Can I start mid-semester?
faqs.answer: Yes. Meetings run all term, and there's no point in the calendar where showing up stops making sense.

faqs.question: How much time does it take?
faqs.answer: A general body meeting runs about an hour. Workshops are one-offs. A build team is a couple of hours a week if you want it to be.

faqs.question: I'd like to sponsor or collaborate with the chapter.
faqs.answer: Email the chapter and it'll reach the officers. We're interested in speakers, equipment, and lab collaborations.

steps.heading: What a first meeting looks like
steps.body: Chapter updates, whatever the project teams have working, and usually a speaker or a hands-on segment. People stick around afterward — that's the part worth staying for.

membership.heading: What society membership gets you
membership.lede: The chapter is your local branch of a society with tens of thousands of biomedical engineers. Joining as a student member opens up what the society runs directly.

benefits.title: Scholarships, awards, and travel grants
benefits.body: EMBS runs student awards and travel grants, and IEEE runs scholarships across all its societies. Members apply, and the pools are smaller than you'd expect.

benefits.title: Conferences at member rates
benefits.body: EMBC is the society's flagship conference and one of the largest biomedical engineering meetings anywhere. Members register at reduced rates, students lower still.

benefits.title: The journals
benefits.body: Membership carries IEEE Xplore access to EMBS publications — Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, the Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics, and the rest of the catalog.

benefits.title: Speakers and lecturers
benefits.body: EMBS runs a Distinguished Lecturer program that chapters can draw on, plus member webinars and technical committees you can actually join.

membership.note: Student rates are set by IEEE and change each year. Check the current figure before signing up.
